similarities.point: Both describe the ovolo as a convex architectural moulding.
similarities.quote_britannica: OVOLLO, or Ouvus, in architecture, a round moulding, whole profile, or sweep, in the ionic and compacite capittals, is usually a quadrant of a circle;
similarities.quote_wikipedia: The ovolo or echinus is a convex decorative molding profile used in architectural ornamentation.

similarities.point: Both state the profile is usually a quarter of a circle.
similarities.quote_britannica: is usually a quadrant of a circle; whence it is also commonly called the quartercard.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: Its profile is a quarter to a half of a more or less flattened circle.

similarities.quote_britannica: It is mainly cut with the reproduction of eggs and anchors or arrows heads placed alternately.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: The "egg and tongue" referred to, also known as egg-and-dart, egg-and-anchor, or egg-and-star, refers to alternating egg and V-shapes enriching the surface of the concave ovolo in many early cases.

similarities.point: Both associate the moulding with Ionic capitals.
similarities.quote_britannica: in the ionic and compacite capittals, is usually a quadrant of a circle;
similarities.quote_wikipedia: Ovolo adornment by the egg-and-dart element was used on Ionic capitals by ancient Roman and ancient Greek builders

wiki_only_topics.topic: Comparison with cavetto and compound moldings
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: The fundamental element of ornamental, architectural molding that is concave (rather than convex like the ovolo) is found in cavetto or hollow chamfering moldings, which also usually presents a quarter-round cross-section, albeit concave.
In modern residential applications, the ovolo profile is often used as the inside edge of stile and rail interior and cabinet doors.
